findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:236 — OptimizedCursorPaginator's "advanced feature" branch slices queryset with a negative start_offset (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`), which Django querysets reject (AssertionError: negative indexing not supported), so any call with `enable_advanced_features=True` and offset<0 raises instead of paginating as the comment claims

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:57 — span_count` is only assigned from the return value of the *last* zunionstore call executed; if both merge branches run, the reported span_count is correct, but the variable is silently stale/misleading if only the first branch fires while the second key check races with a concurrent unlink (TOCTOU between `zcard` check and `zunionstore`), potentially double-counting or under/over-evicting relative to true set size at eviction time

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:872 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result lets enable_advanced_features+negative Cursor.offset flow into queryset[start_offset:stop]; Django QuerySet.__getitem__ asserts against negative slice indices, so the "safe negative slicing" comment is false and the feature either crashes (AssertionError->500) or, if assertions are stripped, produces undefined/invalid OFFSET behavior rather than the intended bounded pagination

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — Gating "advanced pagination"/expanded query power on organization_context.member.has_global_access conflates a team-scope/open-membership attribute with an elevated admin permission, letting ordinary members (not just real admins) unlock the negative-offset code path meant for "authorized administrators"

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:56 — New eviction logic (zpopmin when span_count > 1000) has no test exercising a segment exceeding 1000 spans to prove the cap and flushed-data correctness

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — New optimized_pagination query param + permission-gated OptimizedCursorPaginator path has no endpoint test coverage (no test searches for "optimized_pagination")

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:99 — Negative start_offset slicing (queryset[start_offset:stop] with negative start_offset) is untested; Django querysets generally reject negative indexing, so this path is likely to raise at runtime yet is never exercised by tests

tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py — All updated tests use an identical end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0 for every span, so none of them verify zset ordering/dedup semantics when duplicate payloads have different timestamps (a real behavioral difference from the old set-based sadd)

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:900 — Negative `start_offset` passed to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` triggers Django's `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so any admin (superuser or org member with has_global_access, not necessarily superuser) hitting `?optimized_pagination=true` with a crafted negative cursor offset causes an unhandled 500, a DoS vector on the audit log endpoint

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:65 — enable_advanced=request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` grants the "advanced"/negative-offset pagination path to any org member with global access, not just superusers, widening the exposed attack surface beyond what the inline comments ("authorized administrators") imply

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — Feature flag/rollout gate is a raw request query param (`optimized_pagination=true`) rather than a proper feature flag or options check, letting any authorized caller opt into the unreviewed/experimental code path at will

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:44 — When `is_root_span` is true, both zunionstore branches are skipped so `span_count` stays 0 and falls back to `zcard(set_key)`, which is correct only because `set_key` already reflects the root span's own prior entries; verify this is the intended semantics since span_count no longer reflects "count contributed by this insert" but total set size, changing eviction trigger semantics from the original PR title's "insert-time eviction" — plausible but under-explained mismatch between comment and behavior

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:236 — OptimizedCursorPaginator's "advanced feature" branch slices queryset with a negative start_offset (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`), which Django querysets reject (AssertionError: negative indexing not supported), so any call with `enable_advanced_features=True` and offset<0 raises instead of paginating as the comment claims

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:57 — span_count` is only assigned from the return value of the *last* zunionstore call executed; if both merge branches run, the reported span_count is correct, but the variable is silently stale/misleading if only the first branch fires while the second key check races with a concurrent unlink (TOCTOU between `zcard` check and `zunionstore`), potentially double-counting or under/over-evicting relative to true set size at eviction time

adjudication.rationale: The alleged TOCTOU/race between `zcard` and `zunionstore` cannot occur as shown: this is a Redis Lua script, which executes atomically (no concurrent `unlink` can interleave between the `zcard` check and the subsequent `zunionstore`). Also, `span_count` being overwritten by the last `zunionstore` is not stale in the script’s control flow: if one branch runs, `span_count` reflects that `zunionstore` result; if both run, the second `zunionstore` result reflects the final merged `set_key`; if neither runs, it is recomputed via `zcard(set_key)` before eviction.

matched_golden_ids: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.

This matches the golden comment’s described bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — Gating "advanced pagination"/expanded query power on organization_context.member.has_global_access conflates a team-scope/open-membership attribute with an elevated admin permission, letting ordinary members (not just real admins) unlock the negative-offset code path meant for "authorized administrators"

adjudication.rationale: The diff newly gates the “optimized/advanced pagination” path on `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` and, when enabled, passes `enable_advanced_features=True` to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (organization_auditlogs.py). The paginator contains special handling intended to allow negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features` is true (api/paginator.py). However, the diff does not define what `has_global_access` means or whether it is truly equivalent to an admin-only permission, so the claim that “ordinary members” can unlock it is not verifiable from the diff alone. What is verifiable is that a non-superuser member attribute is being treated as sufficient to enable a more powerful code path, which is a concrete permission/intent mismatch concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:56 — New eviction logic (zpopmin when span_count > 1000) has no test exercising a segment exceeding 1000 spans to prove the cap and flushed-data correctness

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new, nontrivial eviction behavior in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` that caps each zset to 1000 members via `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000) end`. In `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py`, the prior Python-side guard that rejected segments with too many spans is removed (the `max_segment_spans` check during loading is deleted), making correctness more dependent on this Redis-side cap. The updated tests in the diff only add `end_timestamp_precise` and adjust for zset scanning; they do not add a case that creates >1000 spans in a segment to assert eviction/capping behavior and flush correctness. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a directly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821 — OptimizedCursorPaginator class has zero test coverage anywhere in tests/ (no unit test instantiates or calls get_result on it)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new nontrivial paginator class `OptimizedCursorPaginator` in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` and wires it into `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get()` behind the `optimized_pagination=true` flag and an admin check. In the shown test changes, only span-buffer/consumer tests are updated; no tests are added that instantiate `OptimizedCursorPaginator` or exercise its `get_result` paths (including the negative-offset/advanced-features branch). While the diff alone can’t prove there are zero tests elsewhere in the repo, it does show new behavior added without corresponding coverage in the touched tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — New optimized_pagination query param + permission-gated OptimizedCursorPaginator path has no endpoint test coverage (no test searches for "optimized_pagination")

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new conditional behavior in `organization_auditlogs.py` (the `optimized_pagination` query param and a permission-gated switch to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`). In the provided PR diff, no tests are added or modified for the organization audit logs endpoint, and the only test changes shown are for spans buffering/consumers. So this newly introduced code path is not covered by any tests visible in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:99 — Negative start_offset slicing (queryset[start_offset:stop] with negative start_offset) is untested; Django querysets generally reject negative indexing, so this path is likely to raise at runtime yet is never exercised by tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces code paths that can slice a Django queryset with a negative start index. In `BaseOffsetPaginator.get_result` it now uses `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset` and then `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, so if `cursor.is_prev` and `cursor.offset` is negative, `start_offset` will be negative. Additionally, the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, then does `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets generally do not support negative slicing, so this is a likely runtime error path, and the diff adds no tests exercising negative offsets/pagination behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py — All updated tests use an identical end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0 for every span, so none of them verify zset ordering/dedup semantics when duplicate payloads have different timestamps (a real behavioral difference from the old set-based sadd)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes span buffering from Redis sets to sorted sets: `p.sadd(...)` becomes `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})` in `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py`, and Lua union logic switches to `zunionstore`/`zcard` plus trimming by score via `zpopmin` in `add-buffer.lua`. This introduces meaningful new behavior: with ZSETs, identical `payload` values become the same member and later `ZADD` calls update the score, affecting ordering and retention when trimming. The updated tests in `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` (and others) all set `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0`, so they do not exercise or validate these new ordering/dedup/score-update semantics compared to the prior `SADD`-based approach.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:900 — Negative `start_offset` passed to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` triggers Django's `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so any admin (superuser or org member with has_global_access, not necessarily superuser) hitting `?optimized_pagination=true` with a crafted negative cursor offset causes an unhandled 500, a DoS vector on the audit log endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (added in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`), when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing asserts against negative slice bounds (negative indexing not supported), so a crafted negative `cursor.offset` can raise an `AssertionError` and likely produce an unhandled 500. The audit log endpoint enables this paginator when `?optimized_pagination=true` and `enable_advanced` is satisfied (`request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`), and `Cursor.offset` is explicitly allowed to be negative (`self.offset = int(offset)` with no validation in `utils/cursors.py`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:65 — enable_advanced=request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` grants the "advanced"/negative-offset pagination path to any org member with global access, not just superusers, widening the exposed attack surface beyond what the inline comments ("authorized administrators") imply

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new gate is `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, and when combined with `optimized_pagination=true` it enables `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`. This does extend the “advanced” pagination path beyond superusers to any member with `has_global_access`, which may or may not match the intent implied by the inline comments (“authorized administrators”). The diff alone doesn’t prove this is a security/correctness defect (we can’t verify what `has_global_access` signifies), but it is a concrete review concern about authorization scope/comment mismatch. (Also, the finding’s file/line reference to `src/sentry/api/paginator.py:65` doesn’t match where the gate is introduced.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:895 — Comment "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is factually false — Django querysets explicitly reject negative indices — so the entire "safe" justification for the negative-offset feature is incorrect and the code cannot work as documented

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` the new branch explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `cursor.offset < 0` and then performs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (negative slice start). Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and raises an error, so the comment "underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is incorrect and the negative-offset path will break at runtime when triggered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — Feature flag/rollout gate is a raw request query param (`optimized_pagination=true`) rather than a proper feature flag or options check, letting any authorized caller opt into the unreviewed/experimental code path at will

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly gates the new code path on a raw query parameter: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` and then enables it for `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. This means any caller who meets `enable_advanced` can toggle into the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` behavior at will, rather than being controlled by a centralized feature flag/options mechanism. That’s a concrete rollout/operational control concern introduced by the change, but not a directly verifiable correctness/security defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:44 — When `is_root_span` is true, both zunionstore branches are skipped so `span_count` stays 0 and falls back to `zcard(set_key)`, which is correct only because `set_key` already reflects the root span's own prior entries; verify this is the intended semantics since span_count no longer reflects "count contributed by this insert" but total set size, changing eviction trigger semantics from the original PR title's "insert-time eviction" — plausible but under-explained mismatch between comment and behavior

adjudication.rationale: In add-buffer.lua, when `is_root_span` is true the first merge branch is skipped, so `span_count` remains 0 and then is set to `zcard(set_key)`. However `span_count` is only used to decide whether to evict (`if span_count > 1000 then ...`), and both `zunionstore` and `zcard` represent the total cardinality of `set_key` after any merges, not “count contributed by this insert”. The diff does not show any reliance on “insert-time eviction” semantics, nor that correctness depends on `set_key` already containing prior root-span entries; using total set size for eviction works regardless.
